messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-proxy.p99_latency > 1200ms in eu-west-1 for last 5m. SLO risk (p99 target 800ms). Paging eng-sre oncall. Dashboard: https://redwood.ops/alerts/1755009999

riley: saw this. confirming impact — are clients seeing stalls or just higher tails?

alex: we're seeing chunked responses stall at client side, SSE and websocket both. p95 also climbed to ~450ms but p99 is exploding. logs show a few connections with long write queues.

meera: repro looks like proxy write backlog + downstream socket EWOULDBLOCK. sounds like slow consumer problem + proxy keepalive timing interacting with our continuous batching.

samir: possible cause: new batching bump yesterday bumped max inflight tokens to 4x on some pools. might increase KV pressure and per-req serialization time. rolling back is an option but will need a quick rollback plan.

riley: oncall steps: 1) throttle new streaming requests 2) bump proxy write timeout + enable smaller chunks 3) identify top N heavy clients and apply token limits. who can push throttling rule now?

meera: I can push a temporary routing rule to limit concurrent streams per client to 4. quick nginx snippet: ```limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=stream_addr:10m; limit_conn stream_addr 4;``` but our proxy is Envoy — will translate.

alex: Envoy config patch ready, can hot-restart via control plane. will apply to eu-west pool and monitor. doing config roll now.

infra-bot: Deploy started: envoy-config/rollout/1755009999 -> eu-west-1-proxy-pool. ETA ~30s.

maya: quick customer check — Support queue shows a spike in streaming error reports for two customers (HealthCo, DocsFlow). they report partial transcripts and reconnect loops. severity: high for DocsFlow (PLG customers). notifying account reps.

riley: good catch. add DocsFlow to incident impact list. alex/meera, any chance we can open a fallback route to less-optimized model instance (smaller batch) for affected customers? that would reduce per-request latency.

meera: yes, we have a compatibility variant (quantized small-batch) in the catalog. can create a routing rule for requests with header `x-customer: docsflow` to the small-batch model. doing that now.```curl -X POST https://controlplane.local/routes -d '{"match": {"header": "x-customer", "value": "docsflow"}, "route_to": "model-smallbatch-v2"}'```

alex: Envoy throttle rolled out. early telemetry: write queue length dropping ~30% and p99 trending down to ~950ms. still above SLO but moving.

riley: good. continue monitoring. also add more verbose socket stats for the proxy to see stalled connections. alex, toggle trace-level for `proxy.socket_writer`?

alex: toggled. logs will be noisy, sending filtered view: ```[proxy.socket_writer] conn=172.20.5.12 qlen=16384 idle=220s writes=0 last_write=220s``` multiple entries with large idle.

meera: those are slow consumers — client not reading. could be client-side bottleneck or network flaps. recommend we enable shorter chunk flush (split 32kb -> 6kb) so any client that can read small chunks makes progress. I'll flip that in the runtime.

samir: rolling that chunk-size change is low-risk. meera, do it and we'll watch for connection churn.

meera: applied smaller-chunk flush. metric `stream.chunk_size` changed from 32768 -> 6144. infra-bot: config updated.

infra-bot: Action completed: runtime/flush-chunk-size/1755009999 applied across eu-west pool.

riley: telemetry 90s after chunk change: p99 -> 780ms, p95 -> 400ms, #stalled_conns dropped 65%. we're under SLO now but keep watch for customer errors and repeated reconnects.

maya: DocsFlow confirms partial fix — reconnects reduced, but one client still seeing timeouts. collecting app logs.

oncall-night: I'm taking handoff for overnight. summary: incident caused by slow consumer + proxy config interacting with larger batching. mitigation: Envoy per-client concurrency cap + route critical customer to small-batch model + reduce chunk size. current status: stable with p99 ~720ms. please add any remaining actions for night.

riley: thanks. action items for night: 1) keep throttling rule until we validate client fixes, 2) follow up with product for batching revert in next deploy if telemetry regresses, 3) reach out to DocsFlow for client-side flushing guidance + temporary SDK patch.

alex: I'll keep socket tracing on for 4h and collect PCAP samples for a few affected IP ranges.

meera: I'll prepare a controlled rollback plan for the batching bump (safe revert + smoke tests).

samir: I'll open a PR with recommended default chunk size change and a tuning guide in runbooks. link: https://git.internal/runbooks/streaming-chunk-tuning

maya: I've updated the incident ticket with customer impact and mitigation steps. will coordinate postmortem sync.

oncall-night: noted. if things spike I should be @paged. leaving note for follow-ups. good job team :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. created incident: INC-1755009999. severity: Sev2.
